accuracy.reason: Routing, selection, health sampling, affinity, draining and duplicate-safe effects retain the important limits; the documented all-unhealthy exception prevents an absolute health guarantee. Diagrams are consistent.

evidence.quote: Check the product's all-unhealthy policy too. Some balancers send traffic to unhealthy targets when every target fails its checks, rather than refusing all traffic.

mechanisms.reason: Explains selection unit, old connections admitting new requests, in-flight deadline interruption and a cross-backend atomic retry record, so operations and failures are traceable.

evidence.quote: Stopping new L4 connections does not stop new HTTP requests on existing connections. A drain must also manage those connection lifetimes or stop accepting further requests. L7 request-aware draining must still track already accepted work.

coherence.reason: One Notes request connects entry path, routing policy, health, state, deployment, retries and capacity. All eight card objectives and their criteria are supported in order, with database transaction prerequisite stated.

evidence.quote: In this reverse-proxy example, the client contacts one service entry point. The balancer forwards the request to a selected backend. That server reads the note from the database and returns a response through the balancer to the client.

decisions.reason: Policy recommendations are conditional on durations/capacity and measurement; one-server alternative, affinity cost, overload limits and alternate entry path support actual decisions.

evidence.quote: For long, uneven work, consider least connections; for unequal server capacity, consider weights. Check actual latency and resource use before deciding: no policy is universally best.

clarity.reason: Backend, L4/L7, termination, readiness, stickiness, in-flight work, key/deduplication and headroom are defined where needed; concrete examples expose limits without advanced infrastructure detail.

evidence.quote: A stable ID for one logical operation, reused on every attempt. Deduplication means recognizing a repeat. A new key per retry, or a key remembered only in A's memory, cannot reliably protect a retry on B.

sourceChecks.claim: AWS ELB overview supports distributing traffic to registered targets through an entry point; NGINX proxy example confirms forwarded HTTP behavior. Single-server tradeoff is a qualified design choice.

Microsoft distinguishes L4 TCP/UDP from L7 path-routing and TLS offload; connection reuse and need for readable HTTP explain per-connection versus per-request selection. Backend encryption is separately configured.
NGINX defines round-robin, active least-connections and weighted share, and notes unequal request duration and session persistence. Counts/weights are not a universal work or latency guarantee.

AWS health reference explicitly gives periodic intervals, thresholds and all-targets-unhealthy fail-open. Lesson correctly calls checks samples and distinguishes selection removal from completing in-flight work.

Microsoft web-farm reference identifies shared session/cache needs and inconsistent local resources across nodes; NGINX stickiness chooses a server except on unavailability, without replicating memory. Shared dependency costs remain.

AWS deregistration delay stops requests and permits in-flight completion within a wait, with errors from premature termination. General L4 connection/request distinction is correctly carried into the example; no migration or zero-interruption guarantee.

AWS idempotency source explicitly requires stable identifier and ACID recording of token plus all mutations, preserving equivalent results; supports durable atomic deduplication across backends and warns retries need safety.

Google SRE overload chapter states balancing eventually reaches resource limits, caps sent traffic by capacity and requires graceful errors under extreme load. Survivor headroom/shared bottleneck and reachable entry requirements follow from the full serving path.
